mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months compresses equity discount rates and increases liquidity, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate accommodative policy support.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for three consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profit visibility, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based consumer demand contraction that triggers recession fears and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing supply shock regime (INDPRO below 95 for three consecutive months) reduces corporate output and increases input costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to profit margin compression.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO remains below 95 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly non-farm payrolls increase above 150,000 consistently signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 150,000.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL (YoY > 3.0%) and decline in FEDFUNDS (below 2.0%) indicates policy misalignment where inflation rises while rates stay low, creating market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS < 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth above 2.5% for two consecutive quarters), S&P 500 returns turn negative over 60 days as valuations become stretched and policy tightening risks increase.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive quarters.
